title: PipeInfer: Accelerating LLM Inference using Asynchronous Pipelined Speculation
problem: Speculative inference techniques reduce memory bandwidth bottlenecks but increase end-to-end latency and require high speculation acceptance rates; variable acceptance rates combined with pipeline-parallel designs that need many requests reduce performance, especially with low-bandwidth interconnects.
motivation: Efficient distributed LLM inference across clusters requires techniques that tolerate variable speculation acceptance rates and work well for single-request scenarios.
method: PipeInfer employs Continuous Asynchronous Speculation that runs single-token inference simultaneously with multiple speculative runs to improve latency and generation speed. It uses Early Inference Cancellation to skip computation of invalidated speculative runs even mid-inference. The pipelined design reduces inter-token latency and improves system utilization while tolerating low acceptance rates.
key_novelty: Coupling continuous asynchronous speculation with early inference cancellation enables pipelined speculative execution that effectively handles single requests and low speculation acceptance rates.
contributions: Continuous Asynchronous Speculation mechanism for overlapping single-token and speculative inference
Early Inference Cancellation technique to skip invalidated runs mid-computation
Improved generation speed and latency for single-request inference scenarios
Enhanced robustness to low speculation acceptance rates and low-bandwidth interconnects
primary_theme: Asynchronous pipelined speculation for LLM inference
